phases.name: Pure local-write watermark helpers (RCA Solution A foundation: HLC stamp, adoption rule, v2 mirror envelope)
phases.description: Lays the functional core that every adapter step builds on, so the recency decision is a pure, exhaustively tested function rather than four hand-rolled comparisons. RCA section 6.1 option (c): a client-generated hybrid-logical-clock writtenAt (plain ms number, writtenAt = max(now, lastSeen + 1)) stored on the Firestore document AND in the mirror, compared on the client clock only (no serverTimestamp(), D1). Section 6.2: a missing watermark on EITHER side means no comparison (today's server-wins behaviour, D2 part ii); ties adopt; only server < mirror re-pushes. Section 6.3: mirror key bumps to firestore-cache:v2:{uid}:{doc} with a uniform { value, writtenAt } envelope; v1 is read as a watermark-less fallback and its key is removed on every v2 write (D2 part i). ORDERING RATIONALE: helpers ship first and alone because both adapter steps import them, and because the truth table is the one place in this delivery where the invariant can be pinned exhaustively rather than by example. Functional paradigm: exported functions, no classes, no module state. Contract shapes (design-time classification): nextWrittenAt / resolveAdoption / extractWrittenAt / encode-decode are pure-function (return-only, no I/O); readMirrorEnvelope / writeMirrorEnvelope are the thin imperative shell and are the ONLY functions in the module that touch AsyncStorage (bounded-change: exactly the v2 key written and the v1 key removed, nothing else).

steps.name: local-write-watermark.ts: HLC stamp, adoption rule, writtenAt extraction, v2 envelope with v1 fallback, key builders
steps.description: New module src/adapters/firestore/local-write-watermark.ts per RCA section 7 'Shared pure helpers'. nextWrittenAt(now, lastSeen): max(now, (lastSeen ?? -Infinity) + 1) - the clock is injected, never read inside, so the helper is pure and the clock-goes-backwards case is testable without fake timers. resolveAdoption(serverWrittenAt, mirrorWrittenAt): 'repush' only when both are numbers and server < mirror; 'adopt' otherwise (either side null, equal, or server newer). extractWrittenAt(data): the writtenAt field of a snapshot's data() as a finite number, else null (undefined data, missing field, non-number, NaN, non-finite all yield null). Key builders for v1 and v2 per document name (trip, carryover, staples, areas, sectionOrder). readMirrorEnvelope(uid, doc, parseV1, validateV2): v2 key first - a parseable v2 envelope whose value passes validateV2 wins (v1 ignored even if present); an absent OR unparseable v2 falls through to the v1 key parsed by the adapter-supplied parseV1 and wrapped as { value, writtenAt: null }; nothing usable on either key yields null. A v2 envelope with value null and a numeric writtenAt (section order's mirrored clear) is a PRESENT envelope, not 'no entry'. writeMirrorEnvelope(uid, doc, value, writtenAt): fire-and-forget setItem of the v2 JSON envelope plus removeItem of the v1 key on every call (RCA 6.3 'definite rule': a stale v1 value must never mask a v2 write failure on a later launch).
steps.criteria: GIVEN nextWrittenAt WHEN lastSeen is null THEN the result is now; WHEN lastSeen < now THEN now; WHEN lastSeen equals now or lastSeen > now (device clock stepped backwards) THEN lastSeen + 1; AND for any sequence of clock readings that includes backwards steps, feeding each result back as lastSeen yields strictly increasing stamps. GIVEN resolveAdoption WHEN either side is null ((null,null), (null,5), (5,null)) THEN 'adopt' with no comparison; WHEN equal (5,5) or server newer (6,5) THEN 'adopt'; WHEN server older (4,5) THEN 'repush' - the full present/missing x older/equal/newer partition is enumerated. GIVEN extractWrittenAt WHEN data is undefined, {}, { writtenAt: 'x' }, { writtenAt: NaN } or a non-finite number THEN null; WHEN { writtenAt: 42 } THEN 42. GIVEN readMirrorEnvelope WHEN v2 is present THEN its value and stamp are returned and a co-present v1 value is ignored; WHEN v2 is absent and v1 is present THEN parseV1's result is returned with writtenAt null for each adapter shape (raw trip, raw carryover array, raw staple array, raw area array where [] yields null, section-order { order: null } yields { value: null, writtenAt: null }); WHEN v2 holds { value: null, writtenAt: 7 } THEN { value: null, writtenAt: 7 } (present envelope); WHEN v2 is unparseable THEN it falls through to v1, and to null when v1 is also absent. GIVEN writeMirrorEnvelope WHEN called THEN AsyncStorage.setItem was called with the v2 key and a JSON envelope carrying exactly { value, writtenAt } AND AsyncStorage.removeItem was called with the v1 key. All cases are RED before the module exists and GREEN after; no other file changes.
acceptance_criteria: nextWrittenAt returns now when lastSeen is null or behind now, and lastSeen + 1 when lastSeen is equal to or ahead of now; successive stamps are strictly increasing even when the injected clock steps backwards
resolveAdoption enumerates the full truth table: any null side adopts; equal adopts; server newer adopts; only server-older-than-mirror re-pushes
extractWrittenAt yields null for undefined data, a missing field, a non-number, NaN or a non-finite number, and the number itself otherwise

readMirrorEnvelope prefers a valid v2 envelope, falls back to the adapter-supplied v1 parser with writtenAt null, keeps the area rule that an empty or non-array value is no usable mirror, and treats { value: null, writtenAt: <number> } as a present envelope
writeMirrorEnvelope writes the v2 key and removes the v1 key on every call
The module exports functions only (no classes, no module-level mutable state) and imports nothing from the four adapters
steps.scenario_name: Watermark helpers: HLC monotonicity under a backwards clock, adoption truth table, v2 envelope read/write with v1 fallback per adapter shape
steps.implementation_notes: RED first: write the test file against the not-yet-existing module. Use the same AsyncStorage jest mock the adapter unit tests already rely on (firestore-trip-storage.test.ts calls AsyncStorage.clear() in beforeEach) and clear it between cases; for writeMirrorEnvelope spy on AsyncStorage.setItem / removeItem (jest.spyOn) rather than reading keys back, since the write is fire-and-forget. TEST PARADIGM (property in spirit): the project's PBT default applies to this step, but fast-check is NOT a dependency and must not be added, so express each invariant as an exhaustive test.each matrix over the full input partition (present/missing x older/equal/newer for resolveAdoption; null / behind / equal / ahead for nextWrittenAt; the five extractWrittenAt inputs; the five adapter v1 shapes for readMirrorEnvelope) and check HLC monotonicity over a fixed clock sequence such as [100, 100, 50, 200, 150] by folding each output back in as lastSeen and asserting strict increase. phases.name: Recency-gated adoption and mirror re-push in the four Firestore adapters (RCA Root Causes A and B; C resolved by consequence)
phases.description: Closes the defect end to end. Every local write is stamped with nextWrittenAt(Date.now(), <doc>WrittenAt) and the stamp travels on the setDoc payload ({ trip, writtenAt }, { items, writtenAt }, { items: areas, writtenAt }, { order, writtenAt }) and in the v2 mirror envelope. On every data-bearing snapshot, after the existing absent-snapshot guard and the existing content-equality short-circuit, resolveAdoption(extractWrittenAt(data), <doc>WrittenAt) decides: ADOPT (today's path: cache = server value, record the server stamp, disarm the guard, mirror v2 with the server stamp, onChange) or REPUSH (keep the cache, setDoc the cached value with the mirror's own stamp - re-used, not bumped, so the re-push is idempotent - disarm the guard, no onChange, return). Root Cause B is closed by the same mechanism: 'mirror newer than server' IS 'un-acknowledged local write', so no dirty flag or journal is needed (RCA 4 Branch C, Solution C). The D4 disarm rule is UNCHANGED (RCA 6.7): only a data-bearing snapshot disarms the absent-snapshot guard, local writes never touch it, and both ADOPT and REPUSH disarm because in both the server has spoken with data. Hydration reads the v2 envelope with v1 fallback and seeds <doc>WrittenAt; the readiness predicate from fix-slow-render-flaky-network is unchanged in meaning (an envelope from either key counts as 'mirror yielded an entry'). BATCHING DECISION: two steps, not four and not one. The trip adapter is its own step because it owns TWO documents with structurally different handlers (the carryover handler today has no init gating and no echo compare and must gain a content-equality short-circuit before the watermark check, RCA S2/7), its unit test file is the only one whose setDoc mock publishes (S20), and it repairs three of the eight payload assertions. Staples, areas and section order are batched because RCA section 7 shows the identical insertion point in all three (after guard, init, echo; before the adopt block at staple 118 / area 143 / section-order 150), with only the section-order envelope (value: string[] | null, inner { order } wrapper dropped in v2) as a per-adapter nuance. Trip goes first so the regression file's describe.each table is established on the adapter with the richest semantics; the three F1 rows then slot in. Case (c) 'v1 mirror behaves as today' is pinned in EACH step for that step's documents, because each step ships the v1 key deletion for its own documents.

steps.name: Trip and carryover: stamp local writes, gate adoption on the watermark, re-push a newer mirror, v2 envelope with v1 fallback
steps.description: RCA section 7 trip rows. Replace the v1 key builders (37-41) with the helper's builders; persistTripInBackground / persistCarryoverInBackground (43-57) take writtenAt and send { trip, writtenAt } / { items, writtenAt }; mirror writers and readers (59-92) become readMirrorEnvelope / writeMirrorEnvelope with the existing parse bodies passed as parseV1 (trip 72-80, carryover 82-92). Closure state gains tripWrittenAt and carryoverWrittenAt (the watermark of the cached value, null when unknown); commitLocalTripChange / commitLocalCarryoverChange (143-153) mint writtenAt = nextWrittenAt(Date.now(), <doc>WrittenAt), store it, and pass it to both persist and mirror. handleTripSnapshot (155-186): after the guard at 169-171 and the content compare at 173-176, apply the adoption rule; ADOPT records the server stamp and mirrors v2; REPUSH sets tripHydratedFromLocal = false, re-pushes cachedTrip with tripWrittenAt, and returns without onChange. The first-snapshot branch (160-164, no mirror) also records the server stamp. handleCarryoverSnapshot (188-206): add a content-equality short-circuit BEFORE the watermark check (today it re-mirrors unconditionally, S2), then the same ADOPT/REPUSH split. Hydration (214-227) reads both envelopes and seeds both stamps. Regression cases (a) (b) (c) (d) for the trip and carryover rows of the new describe.each table, plus repair of the three trip unit-test payload assertions.
steps.criteria: GIVEN adapter A saved trip V0 then edited to V1 (its last setDoc carried writtenAt W1, a finite number) and adapter B cold-starts under 'delayed' with the mirror hydrated WHEN an older data-bearing snapshot { trip: V0, writtenAt: 1 } is delivered THEN B.loadTrip() equals V1 AND onChange was not called AND exactly one additional setDoc for the trip doc path was issued with { trip: V1, writtenAt: W1 } AND a later cold-start adapter C (mode 'immediate', remote doc forgotten) hydrates V1 - case (a). GIVEN the same setup WHEN a newer snapshot { trip: V2, writtenAt: Date.now() + 1e6 } is delivered THEN B.loadTrip() equals V2, onChange was called once, B issued no setDoc, and adapter C hydrates V2 - case (b). GIVEN AsyncStorage seeded DIRECTLY with a pre-upgrade v1 mirror (raw Trip JSON under firestore-cache:v1:{uid}:trip holding V1) and B under 'delayed' WHEN { trip: V0, writtenAt: 1 } is delivered, and in a second case an unstamped { trip: V0 } THEN B.loadTrip() equals V0 in both, B issued no setDoc, adapter C hydrates V0, and after pending writes settle the v1 key is gone - case (c). GIVEN case (a) has re-pushed WHEN the echo { trip: V1, writtenAt: W1 } is delivered twice THEN the setDoc call count is unchanged, onChange still not called, B.loadTrip() still V1; AND WHEN an absent snapshot is then delivered THEN B.loadTrip() is null, exactly as firestore-trip-offline-cold-start.test.ts:199-202 pins today (the guard stood down on the data-bearing snapshot) - case (d). The same four cases hold for the carryover document (saveCarryover V0 then V1; server field items; silence value []), with the onChange assertions omitted because the carryover handler never fires onChange. Cases (a) and (d) MUST be RED against the current adapter (today B adopts V0, re-mirrors it, and issues no setDoc). The three trip unit tests at lines 132-135, 212-215, 243-246 pass with their payload assertions widened to carry writtenAt: expect.any(Number). Every existing trip regression test (including the unstamped-server-wins tests at 185-210 and 275-294 and the D4 late-empty-snapshot tests), the remaining trip unit tests, migration and acceptance tests stay green unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: An offline trip edit whose mirror stamp is newer than the server document's survives the older data-bearing snapshot in memory, is re-pushed once to Firestore with its own stamp, and is what a later cold start hydrates (case a, trip and carryover)
A server document with a newer stamp still replaces the mirrored value, fires onChange once (trip), and is re-mirrored for the next cold start (case b, trip and carryover)

A pre-upgrade v1 mirror with no stamp behaves exactly as today against both a stamped-older and an unstamped server document: server wins, no re-push, the mirror is migrated to v2 and the v1 key is removed (case c, trip and carryover)
A re-push never loops on its own echo: two echoes with the same stamp issue no further setDoc and no onChange (case d, trip and carryover)

The D4 disarm rule is unchanged: both ADOPT and REPUSH stand the absent-snapshot guard down, local writes still never touch it, and an absent snapshot after a data-bearing one is honoured; all existing disarm tests in firestore-trip-offline-cold-start.test.ts pass unchanged

Every local trip and carryover write sends writtenAt as a finite number on the setDoc payload and in the v2 mirror envelope; the three unit-test payload assertions at trip test 132-135, 212-215, 243-246 are repaired with writtenAt: expect.any(Number) added to the exact-payload literal (not loosened to objectContaining)

Unstamped server documents are adopted exactly as today (S18 regression tests at 185-210 and 275-294 unchanged and green); the carryover handler gains a content-equality short-circuit so an echo no longer re-mirrors
steps.scenario_name: Stale server after process restart: the newer mirrored edit wins, is re-pushed once, and does not loop on its echo (trip and carryover rows)
steps.implementation_notes: RED first. NEW regression file reusing the shared harness exactly as the two sibling regression files do (jest.mock('firebase/firestore', () => require('./helpers/offline-firestore-harness').firestoreModule); resetOfflineFirestore + AsyncStorage.clear in beforeEach; require() the adapter module per createAdapter call). The harness needs NO change: deliverSnapshot accepts { trip, writtenAt } as-is (S16), and firestoreModule.setDoc is the jest.fn to count on - it is not exported under the name mockSetDoc, so import firestoreModule and read firestoreModule.setDoc.mock.calls, filtering by docRef.path. Build the file as describe.each over a row table so 02-02 only appends rows: each row supplies a factory (db, uid, onChange) => adapter, the doc path, the server field name ('trip' | 'items' | 'order'), three distinct values V0 V1 V2, a write(adapter, value) function, a read(adapter) function, the adapter's silence value for the (d) tail (trip null, carryover []), and whether the row asserts onChange. Capture W1 as the writtenAt of A's last setDoc call for that path BEFORE creating B. Use real Date.now(); no fake timers (a stamp of 1 is older than any real clock, Date.now() + 1e6 is newer). Case (c) is the ONE place a test writes an AsyncStorage key directly (it simulates a pre-upgrade device); seed the raw v1 shape (JSON Trip for trip, JSON array for carryover), and the v1-key-removed assertion is acceptable in the same test as a getItem on that already-touched key after settlePendingReads(). UNIT TEST repairs: lines 132-135, 212-215, 243-246 - change the payload literal to { trip, writtenAt: expect.any(Number) } / { items, writtenAt: expect.any(Number) } / { items: [], writtenAt: expect.any(Number) }; keep the exact-literal form so an accidental extra field still fails (RCA 8). The trip unit-test mock publishes writes (S20), so echo tests receive the stamped doc back and hit the equal-content short-circuit - no other unit test changes expected. GREEN: apply RCA section 7 trip rows; the comparison key is the watermark of the cached value (null after adopting an unstamped document) while the HLC floor for the next local stamp is the highest stamp ever observed and is never lowered by adopting an unstamped document (RCA 6.2 is authoritative over the section 7 shorthand; whether that is one closure value or two is the crafter's call). Snapshot data() casts widen to { trip: Trip; writtenAt?: number } etc.; extractWrittenAt tolerates absence. Keep initialize()'s compound readiness predicate (both envelopes present, from either key). Do NOT touch docs/product/architecture/brief.md in this step (02-02 folds the docs touch in once all four adapters carry the pattern). CONTRACT SHAPE: the adapter is bounded-change - its declared mutation set is the in-memory cache, the two stamps, the guard flags, one setDoc per local write or re-push, and the v2/v1 keys of its own two documents; nothing else may change, and the regression assertions go through the port surface only. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: cold-start sequencing and snapshot ordering are single-example integration concerns; the property-level coverage lives in 01-01's exhaustive matrices; src/adapters/ is outside the Stryker scope; fast-check is not a dependency and must not be added. Accepted residuals recorded in RCA 9 and not mitigated here: R1 clock skew in a both-offline race, R2 far-future clock (self-healing), R5 residual window until the doc's first online write, R7 at most one extra write per doc per cold start. COMMIT: 'fix(offline-edit-stale-server): gate trip and carryover adoption on a local-write watermark and re-push a newer mirror' with trailer 'Step-ID: 02-01'; no co-author trailer.

GIVEN adapter A saved order O then cleared it (mirror v2 { value: null, writtenAt: W }) and adapter B cold-starts under 'withheld' WHEN nothing is delivered THEN B.initialize() resolves (envelope present) and B.loadOrder() is null; AND under 'delayed' WHEN an older { order: O, writtenAt: 1 } is delivered THEN B.loadOrder() is still null and exactly one re-push { order: null, writtenAt: W } was issued - a clear is a stamped decision and beats an older server order - case (e). Cases (a), (d) and (e) MUST be RED against the current adapters. validation.note: SCOPE derived from docs/feature/fix-offline-edit-stale-server/deliver/rca.md sections 6-10 with all three decisions approved by the user verbatim: D1 client-generated HLC writtenAt on document and mirror, no serverTimestamp(), comparison on every data-bearing snapshot, server-wins ties; D2 mirror v2 key with uniform { value, writtenAt } envelope (section order drops its inner wrapper), v1 read as stamp-less fallback and removed on first v2 write, missing stamp on either side means no comparison (today's behaviour, residual window R5 accepted); D3 an older offline edit loses to a newer online edit from another device, no refinement. 3 steps / 5 production files (local-write-watermark.ts new, firestore-trip-storage.ts, firestore-staple-storage.ts, firestore-area-storage.ts, firestore-section-order-storage.ts) = 0.6, under the 2.5 ceiling; docs/product/architecture/brief.md is a docs-only touch folded into 02-02 and not counted. ORDERING: 01-01 (pure helpers) strictly precedes both adapter steps, which import it; 02-01 (trip + carryover) precedes 02-02 (staples, areas, section order) because the trip adapter establishes the describe.each row table in the new regression file and carries the richest semantics (two documents, carryover handler with no init gating or echo compare today), so the three structurally identical F1 adapters slot in as rows. BATCHING: two adapter steps rather than four or one - trip separated for its two-document handlers, its publishing unit-test mock (S20) and its own unit file; the three F1 adapters batched under the identical-pattern threshold (same insertion point per RCA section 7: after guard, init, echo; before the adopt block), with the section-order envelope nuance called out explicitly. CASE MAPPING: 01-01 pins the RCA section 7 helper table (nextWrittenAt monotonicity under a backwards clock, resolveAdoption full truth table, extractWrittenAt, per-adapter v1 fallback shapes, present-null envelope, write-plus-remove); 02-01 pins cases (a) (b) (c) (d) for trip and carryover; 02-02 pins cases (a) (b) (c) (d) for staples, areas and section order plus case (e) for the mirrored cleared order. Case (c) appears in BOTH adapter steps rather than only in 02-02 as the task sketch suggested, because each step ships the v1 key deletion for its own documents and the constraint requires the v1-behaves-as-today path to be pinned before that deletion ships; case (d) likewise runs for all five documents (RCA section 8 'run each case for all five documents'), with the post-disarm absent-snapshot tail parameterised by each adapter's silence value (trip null, carryover [], staples [], areas DEFAULT_HOUSE_AREAS, section order null). BREAKING ASSERTIONS repaired (RCA S17, verified by grep to be the only exact setDoc payload literals in the repo; no regression file asserts a setDoc payload): 02-01 repairs firestore-trip-storage.test.ts 132-135, 212-215, 243-246; 02-02 repairs firestore-staple-storage.test.ts 127-130, 141-144, 166-169, firestore-area-storage.test.ts 113-116, firestore-section-order-storage.test.ts 121-124. Repair form is writtenAt: expect.any(Number) added to the exact literal (RCA section 8 prefers this over objectContaining so an accidental extra field still fails). No other existing test changes under D2: the unstamped-server-wins tests (trip regression 185-210, 275-294; mirror regression 193-214, 392-411, 592-611) exercise the missing-server-stamp path and stay green; the mirrored-cleared-order tests (503-512, 534-551) become the R10 guard for the v2 null-value envelope. D4 DISARM RULE UNCHANGED: recorded as an explicit acceptance criterion in 02-01 and 02-02 (both ADOPT and REPUSH disarm; local writes never touch the flag; existing disarm tests unchanged and green). HELPER NAMING follows RCA section 7 (nextWrittenAt(now, lastSeen) with the clock injected, resolveAdoption returning 'adopt' | 'repush') rather than the task sketch's nextWrittenAt(lastSeen) / shouldAdoptServer, because the RCA is the scope contract and injecting the clock keeps the helper pure and makes the backwards-clock case testable without fake timers; the crafter may add a boolean alias if it reads better. PARADIGM: functional TypeScript, factory functions and closures, no classes; fast-check is not a dependency and must not be added - 01-01 applies the PBT default in spirit via exhaustive test.each matrices over the full input partition; the adapter steps are single-example integration tests and exempt; src/adapters/ is outside the Stryker mutation scope by CLAUDE.md policy, so no mutation gate applies. HARNESS: tests/regression/helpers/offline-firestore-harness.ts is reused unchanged (deliverSnapshot accepts stamped payloads; firestoreModule.setDoc is the jest.fn for call counting); the new regression file must not fork it. NO PORT CHANGE: TripStorage, StapleStorage, AreaStorage, SectionOrderStorage and InitializableStorage.initialize are untouched; useAppInitialization.ts has no change. EARNED TRUST NOTE: no probe() is added to the adapters in this delivery - the existing adapters carry none, the RCA does not ask for one, and adding startup probing of AsyncStorage/Firestore is a separate design item recorded here as a follow-up, not folded into a bugfix. ACCEPTED RISKS from RCA section 9, not mitigated here: R1 both-offline clock-skew race (pre-existing LWW, HLC bump orders any edit made after observing the other write), R2 far-future clock (self-healing), R5 residual window until each document's first online write after upgrade, R6 mixed app versions (unstamped docs treated as unknown), R7 at most one extra write per document per cold start. OUT OF SCOPE, explicitly: auth-gate additivity; field-level merges (the only real refinement of whole-document LWW, RCA 6.5); the web persistentLocalCache path - harmless per RCA 6.6 (the durable SDK queue replays the pending write with the mirror's own stamp, and the v1-to-v2 migration runs identically on localStorage), so no platform branch is added; wiring onChange for the section-order adapter in production (S21, UI refresh only); a server-side audit timestamp (may be added later as a separate field that never participates in the comparison). COMMITS: conventional 'fix(offline-edit-stale-server): ...' with a 'Step-ID: NN-NN' trailer, one per step, no co-author trailer.
